definition: A build tool and dev server for front-end projects. It serves your source files with instant updates during development and bundles them into optimized static files in dist/ for production.
A React wrapper component that adds development-only checks, such as rendering components twice and running Effects twice, to expose impure code and missing cleanups. It has no effect in production.
A JavaScript function whose name starts with a capital letter and that returns JSX. You use it like a tag, and React calls it to find out what to show.
A wrapper written as <>…</> or <Fragment> that groups several elements without adding a DOM node, so a component can return siblings as one root.
A syntax extension that lets you write HTML-like markup in JavaScript. A compiler turns each tag into a function call that creates a React element.
A plain JavaScript object, created by JSX, that describes what should appear on screen: a type such as "h2" or a component, plus its props. React turns elements into DOM.
Data calculated during render from props or state, such as a count or a filtered list. It is never stored in state, so it can never drift out of sync with its source.
The inputs a parent passes to a component as attributes, received as one object. Props are read-only: a component never changes them, it receives new ones when the parent re-renders.
The prop that holds whatever is nested between a component's opening and closing tags. Rendering {children} lets a component wrap content it knows nothing about.
A prop that accepts JSX, such as actions={<button>Shuffle</button>}, so the caller decides what appears and the component decides where it goes.
Passing a prop through several components that don't use it, only to reach a deeply nested one. Composition with elements or context can often remove it.
Choosing what a component outputs based on data, using an early return, the ternary operator, or && in JSX. Returning null renders nothing.
When React removes a component from the tree, destroying its DOM and its state. A conditionally rendered component unmounts when its condition becomes false.
A special prop on list items that tells React which item is which between renders. It must be unique among siblings and stable, usually an id from the data.
Data a component remembers between renders, declared with useState. Calling its setter stores a new value and makes React render the component again.
A function whose name starts with "use", such as useState or useEffect, that lets a component use React features. Hooks must be called at the top level of a component.
The fixed set of state values a single render sees. Setting state does not change the current variables; it schedules a new render with new values.
A function passed to a state setter, as in setCount((c) => c + 1). React calls it with the latest pending value, so several updates in a row add up correctly.
Changing state by creating new arrays or objects (with spread, map or filter) instead of modifying the existing ones, so React can detect the change.
A function passed to a prop such as onClick or onSubmit that React calls when the event happens. Handlers are where side effects caused by user actions belong.
The way an event travels from the element where it happened up through its ancestors, triggering their handlers too. e.stopPropagation() stops it.
A form field whose value comes from React state and whose onChange handler updates that state, making state the single source of truth for what the field shows.
A React 19 feature where a function passed to a form's action prop receives the submitted FormData. React prevents the page reload and resets uncontrolled fields afterwards.
A React 19 Hook that wraps an action function and returns the latest result it produced, a dispatch function to pass to a form, and an isPending flag.
Moving state from a component into the closest common parent of every component that needs it, then passing the value down and change handlers down as props.
Code passed to useEffect that runs after React updates the screen, used to synchronize with something outside React such as the document title, storage, timers or subscriptions.
The second argument to useEffect listing every value the Effect reads. React re-runs the Effect only when one of those values has changed since the last render.
A function returned from an Effect that undoes it, such as removing a listener or clearing a timer. React runs it before the Effect runs again and on unmount.
A small CSS class that does one thing, such as p-4 for padding or text-slate-600 for color. Tailwind CSS generates the utilities your files use.
A deployment of a non-production branch or pull request at its own unique URL, so changes can be checked before they are merged and reach the production site.
